about: The unseen UX Randori round (UX-R01, round U). Unlike the worked rounds in randori-rounds.json, no answer to this brief is published: the learner meets the brief cold, the partner holds the sealed card, and a reviewer marks the result against the rubric. tools/ux_review.mjs runs the rows a script can judge on the learner's own flow file. ux_pathway.mjs refuses this file if its brief or its constraint is one of the worked rounds, because then it would not be unseen.

brief.text: A community kitchen: a volunteer books a two-hour cooking slot, is told when the slot clashes with another booking, and can swap to a free slot or give the slot up.
brief.user: A volunteer cook who books the shared kitchen on a phone, often in a hurry between shifts.
brief.job: Get a two-hour slot in the kitchen, and change or give it up when plans change.
mustInclude: the clash: what the volunteer sees when the slot they want is taken, and how they get to a free one
giving a slot up, and what happens to it
at least one error state with its way back
brief.fictional: Kitchen Share is invented for practice. Use invented names and times only; no real kitchen, person or booking.

constraint.text: Nothing takes effect until the volunteer has seen every choice they made on one screen and confirmed it there, and going back from that screen keeps every choice.
constraint.revealAfter: the learner has drawn a first sitemap

flowFormat: Write the sitemap as a flow file in the same format as inputs/pocket-invoice-flow.json: screens, states with their elements, start, and transitions. Mark each transition that takes effect (book, swap, give up) with "commits": true. Give every field the value the volunteer typed or chose.

rubric.criterion: The flow holds together: every state is reachable, nothing is a dead end, every error has a way back, every dialog closes and every button is wired.
rubric.pass: Every listed check passes on the adapted flow file.
rubric.evidence: The flow file and the review sheet that tools/ux_review.mjs writes.

rubric.pass: The constraint check passes on the adapted flow file.

rubric.criterion: The flow does the job in the brief: booking, the clash and the way to a free slot, giving a slot up, and at least one error with its way back.
rubric.pass: The reviewer can point to a state or a transition for each item in the brief's must-include list.
rubric.evidence: The sitemap, with the states named.

rubric.criterion: The learner can say what the constraint changed, and the change is real.
rubric.pass: The learner names the states and transitions the constraint added or removed. With the first flow file given, tools/ux_review.mjs computes them, and the learner's account must agree with that list.
rubric.evidence: Both flow files, and the learner's note of one or two sentences.

rubric.criterion: A partner who did not see the work walks the low-fidelity prototype without help and finishes each task in the brief.
rubric.pass: The partner reaches every goal with no dead end. Every place they stopped or hesitated is written down, with what the learner changed or why they left it.
rubric.evidence: The walk notes: task, where they went, where they stopped.

rubric.criterion: Every error and the clash say what happened and what to do next, in plain words.
rubric.pass: Each error state names the problem and the next step, with no code, jargon or blame.
rubric.evidence: The wireframes of the error states.

rubric.criterion: The screens pass the pathway's QA checklist for wireframes: a visible label on every field, one heading per screen, focus in reading order, a target of at least 24 by 24 px for every control, and no sideways scroll at 320 px.
rubric.pass: Every wireframe passes those items of the QA checklist, or the learner names the item it misses and the fix.
rubric.evidence: The wireframes and the filled QA checklist.

rubric.criterion: The round was done in the time box, without an assistant, and with fictional data only.
rubric.pass: The learner says so on the review sheet; the partner confirms the time.
rubric.evidence: The review sheet, signed by both.

result: Pass when every row passes. A row that does not pass is marked not yet, with the one change that would make it pass; nothing is scored by points.
